newsitem.title: UK: EU aide confirms moves to break air slots impasse.
newsitem.headline: EU aide confirms moves to break air slots impasse.

text.p: The European Commission's competition and transport commissioners are involved in talks aimed at resolving the issue of allowing airline slots to be sold, a senior aide to European transport commissioner Neil Kinnock said on Friday.

But the aide, who requested anonymity, told Reuters by telephone it was wrong to presume that any change in the EU rules banning slot sales would benefit a proposed tranatlantic alliance between British Airways and American Airlines. The aide said allowing BA/AA to benefit from a future rule change on slot sales was "legally impossible".

The UK competition authorities ruled that one of the key conditions for clearance of the BA/AA alliance is to give up 168 slots at its main European airport hub at Heathrow. But the EU has said that slot sales are not allowed under existing rules.

The senior aide confirmed that competiton commissioner Karel Van Miert and Kinnock were examining whether a change in the ban on sales could be introduced allowing slot sales in return for certain requirements to protect competition concerns.
But he stressed even if the change in EU rules was cleared this could not benefit the BA/AA alliance. "The two issues are separate animals and cannot impact on each other," he said.
The Kinnock aide added: "One is the future and the other is the present. We cannot mix the two -- that would be illegal."

It is believed that the BA/AA alliance would therefore be bound by the EU rules at present. He said it was mere coincidence that the two issues clashed with one another, but stressed it was "very important" to keep them separate.
"We will apply the law as it stands and it prohibits the sale of slots," he said.
On future proposals he added: "There are talks between officials on ways of improving the slot regime. We believe it is a good idea to legalise slot sales. But we need safeguards."
